title: Geometric components of an affine scheme descend to a finite constant extension
statement:
Fix a prime power $q$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-pc-base-change]. There exist an integer $e\geq1$ and a finite set $I$ such that, with $k_e=\mathbf F_{q^e}\subset k$, there is a decomposition into nonempty open and closed affine subschemes
$$X_0\times_{k_0}k_e=\coprod_{i\in I}X_{i,e}.$$
Each $X_{i,e}$ is geometrically connected over $k_e$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and their base changes to $k$ are exactly the connected components of $X$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. If $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], each $X_{i,e}\to\operatorname{Spec}k_e$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$. The empty scheme is allowed, with $I=\varnothing$.

mathlib_searches.query: Geometric connected components of a finite type scheme descend to a finite field extension
A finite extension of a finite field splits a smooth affine scheme into finitely many geometrically connected smooth affine components of the same relative dimension
Every affine scheme of finite type over a finite field becomes a finite disjoint union of geometrically connected affine schemes after finite extension of the base field

from.place: Proof, second paragraph: choose a finite extension over which all geometric connected components are defined; the resulting components are smooth affine curves
